operations_plan.summary: Identify the existing horizontal front-panel button and establish a symmetric, collision-free vertical layout for two identical copies.

steps.description: Locate the existing horizontal pill-shaped control on the left side of the +Y-facing upper front control panel. Use feature F-10 and its faces 419-424 as the authoritative source geometry. Resolve the body owning these faces in the CAD assembly; solid 40 is the expected source body, but face ownership should be used to confirm this before copying.

Extract the source button's complete definition, including its body or feature history, local coordinate system, center point, horizontal major-axis orientation, width, height, front-panel offset or insertion depth, edge blends, appearance, and any associated mounting or panel-cut geometry. Preserve the source button without editing it.

Identify the usable local region of the +Y-facing upper front panel surrounding F-10. Reference the +Y-facing exterior face among the rounded enclosure-shell faces 0-11 and account for the central selector F-09, selector scale F-11, position dots F-12, paired status slots F-13, panel seams, and outer panel boundary. Do not alter any of these reference features during layout construction.

Create a construction axis through the center of F-10 parallel to the model Z axis. Because semantic orientation defines -Z as upward and +Z as downward, define the upper-copy center as C_upper = C_original - d·Z and the lower-copy center as C_lower = C_original + d·Z. Select one common positive center-to-center spacing d that fits both copies within the panel, prevents overlap between adjacent buttons, and avoids all neighboring controls. Since no numeric spacing is specified, choose a visually balanced value from the available envelope and apply exactly the same d above and below.

operations_plan.summary: Create the upper horizontal button as an exact translated copy of the existing button.

steps.description: Duplicate the complete source button body or component resolved from F-10. If the source is defined as an additive or subtractive panel feature rather than a standalone component, duplicate the full feature definition, including its pill-shaped profile, depth, rounded ends, blends, and any local mounting clearance, rather than recreating an approximate profile.

Translate the duplicate from the original center to C_upper using vector (0, 0, -d). Do not rotate or scale the copy. Constrain it to the same X coordinate, the same +Y panel offset or insertion depth, and the same horizontal major-axis orientation as the original button.

Attach or integrate the upper copy using the same method as the original. For a separate button body, preserve the same panel seating relation and copy its material, color, and component properties. If the original includes a panel opening, pocket, or mounting recess, reproduce that local interface on the +Y-facing enclosure panel at the translated location while preserving the panel everywhere else.

operations_plan.summary: Create the lower horizontal button as a second exact translated copy of the existing button.

steps.description: Create a second independent duplicate from the original F-10 source definition, not from altered surrounding panel geometry. Preserve the original pill-shaped dimensions, horizontal orientation, projection or recess depth, edge blends, appearance, and any available actuation or component metadata.

Translate the second duplicate from the original center to C_lower using vector (0, 0, +d). Keep its X coordinate, +Y panel offset or insertion depth, scale, and rotation identical to the original and upper copy, producing a single vertical centerline through all three buttons.

Attach or integrate the lower copy by duplicating the original seating and mounting condition. If local panel accommodation is part of the source feature, repeat only that accommodation at the lower translated location. Retain the original button and do not merge the three visible button bodies unless the source modeling method requires them to be unified with the panel.

operations_plan.summary: Validate the completed three-button column and confirm preservation of all non-target geometry.

steps.description: Measure the final button centers and verify that the upper-to-original and original-to-lower center distances are equal to the selected value d within modeling tolerance. Confirm that all three major axes are horizontal, their centers are collinear parallel to Z, and their widths, heights, depths, blends, and appearances match.

Run interference and minimum-clearance checks between both new buttons, the original button, the selector knob and scale, the selector-position dots, the paired vertical status slots, panel seams, and the outer control-panel boundary. If a conflict exists, adjust only the shared spacing d while maintaining symmetric placement about the original button and equal adjacent spacing.

Rebuild the model and verify that the original F-10 button remains unchanged and that no geometry outside the local upper-front-panel button interfaces has moved or changed. In particular, preserve the central brewing group, operating lever, steam wand, cup bay, cups, ribbed panel, retaining rails, chassis, rear shell, ventilation matrix, feet, and all rear, side, top, and bottom features.
